narrative.northStar: The Shop Window on Washington Street
narrative.overview:
Puerto Chill is a real neighborhood shop, and the system is built from the things on its counter: sand and cream walls, a petrol-blue shopfront frame, olive for the hand that takes your order, and kraft-paper price tags tied on with string. It continues the identity of the shop's source PDF (sand grounds, olive, petrol, a Georgia-metric serif) and extends it into a working storefront and a working back office.

The storefront persuades: a serif headline at shop-sign scale, an arched shop window with two shelves of hand-drawn objects, and a catalog laid out as a shelf. The admin operates: the same tokens, the same serif for page titles, but quiet panels, switches and fields, with petrol reserved for the sidebar. One token set serves both; the difference is density and restraint, never a second palette.

Surfaces are flat and warm. Depth comes from tone (sand under paper, petrol bands across the page) and from a few soft, ink-tinted drop shadows on physical objects (shelves, tags, the hanging address tag), not from floating cards. The PDF's tracked uppercase eyebrows above headings were deliberately dropped: headings stand on their own.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and sand grounds; petrol fills whole bands; olive is the only action color.
Gelasio serif for every heading and price-of-the-moment; Hanken Grotesk for all UI.
Kraft tags with a punched hole and string are the brand's badge and price gesture.
1px warm hairlines and 6px corners everywhere; nothing pill-shaped except counts and switches.
Hand-drawn single-stroke icons and product art (1.6px icon stroke, 2.2px art stroke, round caps).
Motion is ease-out-quint, short, and always yields to reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Olive is the only color that means "do this". Petrol never becomes a button fill; at most an outlined link sits on a petrol band.

rules.name: The Whole Band Rule
rules.body: Petrol is applied edge to edge (bars, bands, sidebars, summary blocks), never as a small accent or a text color on light grounds except the active admin nav label.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every price, count and quantity uses tabular figures (`.tnum`).

rules.name: The Headings Stand Alone Rule
rules.body: No tracked uppercase eyebrow or kicker above a heading. The only uppercase tracked text in the system is the "Bazar · Marroquinería" line inside the wordmark lockup, and the announcement bar's light +0.06em tracking.

rules.name: The Cast Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is an object in the shop". Cards, panels, inputs and buttons stay flat with a hairline.

dos: **Do** use Counter Olive (#58633f) for every primary action and nothing else.
**Do** lay petrol (#22414f) as whole bands and frames, edge to edge.
**Do** set headings, product names and featured totals in Gelasio 400 with negative tracking at display sizes.
**Do** use the kraft Tag for badges and price moments, and tabular figures for all money.
**Do** keep corners at 6px and borders at 1px Hairline (#ddd3c3).
**Do** draw icons and product art as single round-capped strokes in Espresso Ink (1.6px icons, 2.2px art).
**Do** animate with ease-out-quint (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)) and keep every motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** give the admin the same tokens as the storefront, quieter: panels, hairlines, switches, sans panel headings.
donts: **Don't** put tracked uppercase eyebrows or kickers above headings; the PDF's eyebrows were dropped on purpose.
**Don't** use petrol as a button fill or kraft as a primary action.
**Don't** add drop shadows to cards, panels, inputs or buttons; shadows belong to shelves, tags and objects.
**Don't** introduce pill-shaped buttons or larger radii outside the shop-window arch.
**Don't** introduce a second accent color or a cool gray neutral; all neutrals are warm.
